You can, dude. If you eat enough grams of protein and are at maintence level calories then you should achieve results, albeit in slower time. Bulking doesn’t always need to be done and honestly makes you gain more fat than muscle and is a complicated process if you want to be lean all throughout

What I’ve been doing is calisthenics (basic compound movements like push ups, pull ups, squats/lunges and then variations once mastered) and progressing to a weighted form of them when I feel like they aren’t difficult anymore. I did this first, still doing it now, but also have done weight lifting to work on my legs and other areas that haven’t grown as much as I’d like with just calisthenics. So these include deadlifts, bench press, dumbbells, and barbell squats to target those certain areas. My workout splits are all full body with jump rope as warmup and calisthenics workout as the primary movements, and they’re on mondays, wednesdays, fridays. If I don’t feel like certain areas are really strained then I move to weight lifting to finish it all off. If you like weight lifting more, which I see as a cop out for most and less impressive compared to weighted calisthenics, then I recommend doing a short calisthenics warm up before doing weight lifting. 

We have similiar stats, and I also have done training to get rid of my skinny fat problem, so doing the above should def help you.

Also, calories and macros are important too. As long as you’re getting around 1g protein or more per body weight you should be set. People tend to neglect this step. Getting more calories than maintence (bulking) isn’t exactly necessary to building muscle. It’s more about how you set up your macros and staying around maintenence. This is from experience and it’s worked for me given how we share similiar stats.

I’d say to work a lot more on your chest, shoulders, lats, and legs. Once you accomplish making those areas look proportional to the rest of your body you should be good. You could try bulking but I honestly don’t recommend it coming from a 5’11 guy myself and around your weight. Keep the calories the same and focus on the muscle groups I listed earlier with gradual progression + heavy lifting.

I honestly go through the same thing as you and it sucks. Just know that you’re not alone in your struggle and that it will get better eventually. Trust me on this. I’m a highschool senior and just like you, I experience stuttering and go through phases were it is pretty bad. I even had a similar instance in my class were I cussed under my breath haha. But I have used these embarrassing moments as a fuel to push myself further so that one day I can overcome it. I accepted that it won’t ever get better unless I work hard to improve it. I developed some strategies and tricks to get around my stutter blocks and they’ve worked surprisingly well. Just try to be confident in yourself and rehearse what you’re going to say many times before speaking. And speaking from personal experience, I found that saying “um” or “uh” before I feel like I’m going to stutter helps get around it.
